passages.text: Jonah, however, was greatly displeased, and he became angry.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
God showed mercy to the people of Nineveh.
Jonah saw this.
Jonah felt very displeased.
Jonah became very angry.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥רַע אֶל־ יוֹנָ֖ה רָעָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיִּ֖חַר לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
Jonah prayed to the LORD.
Jonah said, “O LORD, this is what I said when I was still in my own country.
This is why I hurried to flee to Tarshish.
I knew that You are a gracious God.
You are compassionate.
You are slow to anger.
You are rich in loving devotion.
You relent from sending disaster.”
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֶל־ יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ הֲלוֹא־ זֶ֣ה דְבָרִ֗י עַד־ הֱיוֹתִי֙ עַל־ אַדְמָתִ֔י עַל־ כֵּ֥ן קִדַּ֖מְתִּי לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֑ישָׁה כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ אֵֽל־ חַנּ֣וּן וְרַח֔וּם אֶ֤רֶךְ אַפַּ֙יִם֙ וְרַב־ חֶ֔סֶד וְנִחָ֖ם עַל־ הָרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: And now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live.”
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
Jonah spoke to the LORD.
Jonah said, “O LORD, take my life from me now.
It is better for me to die than to live.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה קַח־ נָ֥א אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֛י ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃ס

passages.text: But the LORD replied, “Have you any right to be angry?”
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to Jonah.\r\nThe LORD asked Jonah a question.\r\nThe LORD said, “Is it right for you to be angry?”

passages.text: Then Jonah left the city and sat down east of it, where he made himself a shelter and sat in its shade to see what would happen to the city.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet.
Jonah left the city.
He went to the east side of the city.
Jonah made a shelter for himself there.
He sat under the shelter.
He sat in the shade.
Jonah waited to see what would happen to the city.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹנָה֙ מִן־ הָעִ֔יר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעִ֑יר וַיַּעַשׂ֩ ל֨וֹ שָׁ֜ם סֻכָּ֗ה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב תַּחְתֶּ֙יהָ֙ בַּצֵּ֔ל עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִרְאֶ֔ה מַה־ יִּהְיֶ֖ה בָּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: So the LORD God appointed a vine, and it grew up to provide shade over Jonah’s head to ease his discomfort, and Jonah was greatly pleased with the plant.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God acted.
The LORD God chose a plant.
The LORD God made the plant grow quickly.
The plant grew above Jonah.
The plant gave shade over Jonah’s head.
The shade protected Jonah from his discomfort.
Jonah saw the plant.
Jonah felt very happy about the plant.
passages.original: וַיְמַ֣ן יְהוָֽה־ אֱ֠לֹהִים קִיקָי֞וֹן וַיַּ֣עַל׀ מֵעַ֣ל לְיוֹנָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת צֵל֙ עַל־ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ לְהַצִּ֥יל ל֖וֹ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ וַיִּשְׂמַ֥ח יוֹנָ֛ה עַל־ הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן שִׂמְחָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃

passages.text: When dawn came the next day, God appointed a worm that attacked the plant so that it withered.
passages.sermon:
God acted the next morning.
Dawn came.
God appointed a worm.
The worm attacked the plant.
The plant withered.
passages.original: וַיְמַ֤ן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ תּוֹלַ֔עַת בַּעֲל֥וֹת הַשַּׁ֖חַר לַֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וַתַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ הַקִּֽיקָי֖וֹן וַיִּיבָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: As the sun was rising, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head so that he grew faint and wished to die, saying, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord over all creation.
God controls the wind and the sun.
Jonah is a prophet.
Jonah is sitting outside the city of Nineveh.
The sun began to rise.
God sent a hot east wind.
The sun struck Jonah’s head.
Jonah became very weak.
Jonah wanted to die.
Jonah said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ וַיְמַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים ר֤וּחַ קָדִים֙ חֲרִישִׁ֔ית וַתַּ֥ךְ הַשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ עַל־ רֹ֥אשׁ יוֹנָ֖ה וַיִּתְעַלָּ֑ף וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר ט֥וֹב מוֹתִ֖י מֵחַיָּֽי׃

passages.text: Then God asked Jonah, “Have you any right to be angry about the plant?” “I do,” he replied. “I am angry enough to die!”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jonah.
God asked Jonah a question.
God said, “Are you right to be angry about the plant?”
Jonah answered God.
Jonah said, “I am right to be angry.”
Jonah said, “I am angry enough to die.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ יוֹנָ֔ה הַהֵיטֵ֥ב חָרָֽה־ לְךָ֖ עַל־ הַקִּֽיקָי֑וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הֵיטֵ֥ב חָֽרָה־ לִ֖י עַד־ מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: But the LORD said, “You cared about the plant, which you neither tended nor made grow. It sprang up in a night and perished in a night.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jonah.
The LORD said, “You cared about the plant.
You did not work for this plant.
You did not make this plant grow.
This plant grew up in one night.
This plant died in one night.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אַתָּ֥ה חַ֙סְתָּ֙ עַל־ הַקִּ֣יקָי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־ עָמַ֥לְתָּ בּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֣א גִדַּלְתּ֑וֹ שֶׁבִּן־ לַ֥יְלָה הָיָ֖ה וּבִן־ לַ֥יְלָה אָבָֽד׃

passages.text: So should I not care about the great city of Nineveh, which has more than 120,000 people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well?”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jonah.
God is merciful and compassionate.
God said, “Nineveh is a great city.
More than 120,000 people live in Nineveh.
These people do not know right from wrong.
Many animals also live in Nineveh.
Should I not care about this great city?”
passages.original: וַֽאֲנִי֙ לֹ֣א אָח֔וּס עַל־ נִינְוֵ֖ה הָעִ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ בָּ֡הּ הַרְבֵּה֩ מִֽשְׁתֵּים־ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה רִבּ֜וֹ אָדָ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ יָדַע֙ בֵּין־ יְמִינ֣וֹ לִשְׂמֹאל֔וֹ וּבְהֵמָ֖ה רַבָּֽה׃
